interframe.page.title: Interframe
interframe.option.enabled.tooltip: Capture each finished frame and insert synthesised in-between frames to raise the perceived frame rate and smooth motion. The benefit is largest when your real FPS sits below your monitor's refresh rate. Works with V-Sync on or off: with it off, frames are spread evenly by the pacing scheduler; with it on, they are slotted into free vblanks automatically.
interframe.option.mode.tooltip: How frames are synthesised. Reproject (recommended): interpolates between the two latest real frames with exact rotational reprojection plus depth-based translation compensation — the smoothest image, at ~1 frame of latency. Timewarp: warps the newest frame FORWARD along your motion so the view leads instead of lags — lowest latency, slight overshoot on direction changes. Blend: plain cross-fade. Neural: a RIFE model via ONNX Runtime for learned interpolation (needs a model + the runtime — see the README).
interframe.option.generated.tooltip: How many synthetic frames to insert between each pair of real frames. 2x inserts one, 3x inserts two, 4x inserts three. Higher multiplies smoothness, but each synthetic frame still costs GPU time, so your real frame rate drops as this rises. With V-Sync on, only as many frames as fit into free vblank slots are actually inserted.
interframe.option.reproject_strength.too: How strongly the camera motion is reprojected (applies to Reproject, Timewarp and Neural). 100% fully warps the image to the synthesised viewpoint (sharpest while moving); lower eases it back toward a plain blend. No effect in Blend mode.
interframe.option.translation_warp.toolt: Compensate camera MOVEMENT (walking, strafing, flying) using the scene depth buffer, not just rotation — this is what keeps the world sharp while you move around instead of ghosting into a double image. Costs one depth copy per frame. Automatically disabled under Iris shaderpacks, where the vanilla depth buffer isn't valid.
interframe.option.look_ahead.tooltip: Timewarp only. How far ahead, in frames, the displayed image is warped along your motion — this is the latency compensation. Higher feels more responsive/snappier while turning, but over-predicts a touch (slight overshoot when you stop or change direction). ~0.50–0.80 is a good range. Has no effect in the other modes.
interframe.option.max_warp.tooltip: If the view rotates more than this in a single frame, the warp is treated as a cut/teleport and skipped (the frame just blends) so respawns and big camera jumps don't smear. Large positional jumps are treated the same way automatically.
interframe.option.pacing.tooltip: How fully the inserted and real frames are spread across the frame interval. Even spacing is what your eyes read as smoothness — without it, synthetic frames are swapped back-to-back and the monitor never even shows them. 100% is perfectly even at the cost of up to half a frame of latency at 2x; 0% presents immediately (lowest latency, but largely defeats frame generation with V-Sync off). Ignored with V-Sync on, where the vblank does the pacing.
interframe.option.in_game_only.tooltip: Only generate frames while you're actually in a world. Leave on; there's nothing moving to interpolate on menus and loading screens.
interframe.option.preserve_hud.tooltip: Keep the held item, hotbar, crosshair and the rest of the HUD out of the warp/blend entirely, so synthetic frames never smear or ghost them — only the world behind them is interpolated. Costs one extra frame capture; leave on unless you're chasing every last bit of headroom.
